text:
Zoe: hi all, first-day network weirdness. VPN connects, can SSH to bastion by IP, but `ssh bastion` tries IPv6 and hangs. `ssh -4 bastion` works. Also `docker pull internal.registry.redwood/my-image` times out unless I force IPv4. Home on an eero mesh with IPv6 enabled. Any ideas?

Ben: welcome Zoe! sounds like your resolver is returning AAAA records and the VPN or bastion doesn't accept v6 traffic from your client. Quick workaround: force ssh to IPv4 with `AddressFamily inet` in `~/.ssh/config` or `ssh -4`. For docker, set `--dns` to an IPv4 corp DNS or add `hosts` entry.

Zoe: added `AddressFamily inet` and ssh is fine. docker still tries AAAA and times out. How do I force Docker Desktop to prefer IPv4?

Clara: two routes: 1) disable IPv6 on your home router/mesh (eero has a toggle) so you only get A records from the resolver; 2) ensure your system resolver returns A-first by configuring `precedence ::ffff:0:0/96 100` (Linux) or use `resolve.conf` tweaks. On Mac/Windows, easiest is to add the internal registry hostname to Docker Desktop's DNS or to `/etc/hosts` with the IPv4 address for dev.

Zoe: I can't change network policy on the mesh (roommate manages it). Is there a per-machine safe fix?

Ben: you can prefer IPv4 for glibc by adding `precedence ::ffff:0:0/96  100` to `/etc/gai.conf` (Linux). On macOS there isn't a direct equivalent; using `networksetup -setv6off Wi-Fi` will turn off IPv6 on the interface. On Windows you can disable IPv6 in adapter settings or via registry; but careful with system-wide changes.

Omar: also check split-tunnel DNS — if your client uses ISP DNS for AAAA queries but corp A records differ, you can get mismatches. If you see AAAA returned but the VPN doesn't route IPv6, that explains the hang. Try `dig +short A internal.registry.redwood` and `dig +short AAAA internal.registry.redwood` to confirm.

Zoe: ran `dig`. Got both A and AAAA; AAAA points to a global v6 that doesn't route over VPN. So docker tries v6 and packets never hit the registry.

Clara: for Docker a pragmatic step: add an entry in `/etc/hosts` mapping internal.registry.redwood to the IPv4 address, and add it to Docker Desktop's 'custom DNS server' setting to avoid DNS leaks. Also add `internal.registry.redwood` to NO_PROXY so proxy doesn't break it.

Zoe: hosts trick worked and docker pull is back. But is this a security risk or something infra should fix centrally?

Omar: infra should ensure corp hostnames either return only v4 addresses to split-tunnel users or have v6 routed via the VPN. We can file a ticket to evaluate returning only A records on the split-tunnel DNS or announce IPv6 routing.

Infra-bot: Automated: created INFRA-5305 "Split-tunnel DNS returns AAAA for internal hosts; investigate IPv6 routing or DNS policy" (https://redwood.internal/infra/5305). See onboarding network notes: https://redwood.internal/onboard/networks (bot).

Ben: follow-ups for your onboarding checklist: 1) add `AddressFamily inet` to `~/.ssh/config` or use `ssh -4`; 2) add internal registry to `/etc/hosts` or Docker Desktop DNS; 3) add `internal.registry.redwood` to NO_PROXY; 4) if you can, ask roommate to disable IPv6 or set eero to hand only IPv4 DNS to your device.

Zoe: thanks all — adding these to my onboarding notes. One last Q: will INFRA-5305 change anything for me in the near term?

Omar: we'll triage. If it's an infra-level change it'll go through the ticket; short-term fixes are per-device as above. I'll add a comment on the ticket referencing this thread.

Zoe: awesome, saved this. Appreciate the quick help! :party_parrot:
